title: Why sepsis bundle delivery differs across five hospitals
subtitle: Barriers and facilitators to timely antibiotics; several facts still to be confirmed
statement: Across five hospitals, delivery of the sepsis bundle, and in particular antibiotics within one hour, is described as reliable at some sites and poor at others, especially at night. The reasons are not known. Understanding the barriers and facilitators at higher- and lower-performing sites comes before choosing strategies to help the weaker sites. The investigator's role, the current performance figures and the resources available are not stated in the request and need to be confirmed.
whoAffected: Adults presenting with suspected sepsis to the five hospitals, the emergency and ward staff who recognise and treat sepsis, and each site's sepsis lead.
whatHurts: Delay to antibiotics in sepsis is linked to worse outcomes, and unexplained variation means that some patients receive slower care depending on where and when they arrive.
currentPractice: A sepsis bundle exists at all five sites; how it is delivered, monitored and supported at each site is not described in the request.
whyNow: Not stated; the variation between sites appears to be known locally, which suggests that performance data exist.
constraints: Not stated: funding, timeline, staff time for fieldwork, approvals and access to performance data are unknown.
patientCenteredGoal: Every adult with sepsis at any of the five hospitals receives antibiotics and the rest of the bundle promptly, day or night.
summary: Problem framed from a brief request; the investigator's role, figures and resources must be confirmed.
